The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondent No.1 and 2 for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 01.06.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. Vanitha G.S. had been proceeding as a pillion rider on bike SCCH 5 bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KL-1102 being ridden by her brother Purushotham on Sondekoppa road, at Byregowdanahalli-Venkatapura, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, a two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q-8726 being ridden by its rider came from opposite direction at high speed in rash and negligent manner and in an attempt to overtake a JCB, he took his vehicle to right side and hit to the bike on which Vanitha G.S. was proceeding, as a result of which, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, Nelamangala, after firstaid she was shifted to Sparsh Hospital,
Yeshwanthapur, Bengaluru, wherein she got operated, thereafter shifted to Hill Home Health Care Hospital, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru, though she was given life saving treatment, she succumbed to the injuries on 23.01.2023 at about 10.35 a.m.

sentences.text: Thereafter SCCH 5 her body was subjected to post mortem at Nelamangala Government Hospital, body was handed over to the petitioners, they performed last rite ceremony and obsequies by spending a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Further petitioners have also spent a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- towards medical and other connected expenses.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Vanitha G.S. was aged about 19 years, she was studying B.Com.,
Petitioner No.1 is mother and petitioner No.2 is father of the deceased, due to untimely death of the deceased, they are suffering from mental shock and agony, pain and suffering, disappointment,
frustration, loss of amenities etc.,
Out of the said accident, crime No.280/2022 and under UDR Nlo.10/2023 is registered before the Madanayakanahalli police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 and 304A of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 SCCH 5 is insurer of the Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q- 8726, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.80,00,000/-
with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/ R.C.Owner has appeared through counsel, but not chosen to file written statement.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement Vanitha G.S vs Rathnamma R on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142129923/

Further submitted that, Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-Q- 8726 was insured with respondent No.2 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, rider of the offending scooter was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to take defence available under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further denied occurrence of SCCH 5 the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, age and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further submitted that, deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident, which is violation of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, deceased was not died due to accidental injuries and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased and her death, as the alleged accident was taken place on 01.06.2022 and deceased was died on 23.01.2023,
so that, deceased was died in her residence due to some other ailment and not due to accidental injuries.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Vanitha G.S. D/o. Shiva Kumar G.V. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.06.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. near Sondekoppa Road, Byregowdanahalli, Vnkatapura, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent riding of Two Wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q-8726 dashed against the deceased travelling on motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

24. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Vanitha G.S. was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.20, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 05.08.2002,
the alleged accident was occurred on 01.06.2022.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.20, age of the deceased is considered about 20 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in SCCH 5 between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.49,38,912/- (Rupees Forty Nine Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand Nine Hundred Twelve Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.
The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

opennyai_summary.facts:
:
The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondent No.1 and 2 for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 SCCH 5 is insurer of the Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q- 8726, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Further submitted that, Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-Q- 8726 was insured with respondent No.2 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, rider of the offending scooter was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to take defence available under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further denied occurrence of SCCH 5 the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, age and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further submitted that, deceased was not died due to accidental injuries and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased and her death, as the alleged accident was taken place on 01.06.2022 and deceased was died on 23.01.2023,
so that, deceased was died in her residence due to some other ailment and not due to accidental injuries.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
MLC Extract is a SCCH 5 primary document, it cannot be thrown out because it has written at the time of the initial stage of the accident and no one has intention to get compensation at that time it was written and after thought petitioner has created the documents and in criminal case proceedings are not binding on MACT court and after hearing the arguments on respondent's side, subsequently petitioners have examined PW-5, who is brother of the deceased and PW-1 has admitted in his cross- examination that,            etc.,
The said evidence of PW-1 indicates to the court that, no vehicle of respondent No.2 insured vehicle has involved in this case and prays to dismiss the petition with exemplary cost.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1.
Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Vanitha G.S. D/o. Shiva Kumar G.V. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.06.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. near Sondekoppa Road, Byregowdanahalli, Vnkatapura, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent riding of Two Wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-52-Q-8726 dashed against the deceased travelling on motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments: 4 MLC Extract that, who has hit the vehicle of the deceased.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further there is no dispute that, during the pendency of the petition,
petitioner has been died on 23.01.2023 out of the injuries caused in the alleged accident dated 01.06.2022. Ofcourse there is no charge sheet has been filed by the Investigation Officer as well as police for the alleged offence under Sec.304(A) of IPC, but there is no dispute about registration of UDR by the police under UDR No.10/2023 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 and Vanitha G.S vs Rathnamma R on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142129923/
5 304A and further there is no dispute with regard to death of the petitioner Vanitha G.S.
14.
So here in this case also, merely petitioner nor her parents have not stated vehicle number in the police intimation and MLC extract are not a sole ground to disbelieve the entire case of the petitioners, because Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.36 documents
clearly indicates to the court with regard to the held of the accident, causing of injuries, taking of treatment by the deceased in several hospitals, but the treatment those taken by the petitioner for the injuries those have caused in the alleged accident have not at all healed and finally the injuries those have caused out of the accident on 01.06.2022 have taken the life of Vanitha G.S. Accordingly any amount of arguments advanced by the Sri.G.S. counsel for respondent No.2 as stated supra have not support the respondent No.2 case in any manner.
Accordingly I am of the opinion that, petitioners have categorically, cogently and corroborately proved their case with regard to the held of the accident as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1 and PW-5.
22.
Accordingly relying on Ex.P.20, age of the deceased is considered about 20 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in SCCH 5 between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
To prove the same,
petitioners have exhibited school records of the deceased marked as Ex.P.21.
27. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.
In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case SCCH 5 of fixed salary employee.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to her age.
29. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.
Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.14,750/-
(ii) 40% of (i) above if Rs.14,750/- (+) added to the Rs.5,900/- = monthly income as Rs.20,650/-
 future prospects (iii) 1/2 of (ii) of the Rs.20,650/- (-)
 same to be deducted Rs.10,325/- =
 towards personal  and living expenses
Monthly income Rs.10,325/- p.m (iv) Compensation after Rs.10,325/- x Rs.22,30,200/-
 multiplier of 18 is 12 x 18  applied  SCCH 5 30.
Further petitioner No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/-
each towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
31. Further it is the case of the petitioners that, deceased Vanitha G.S. has sustained severe head injury, right temporal contusion, left FTP SDH, aspiration pneumonia, which is grievous in nature.
Further she took treatment as inpatient at Truelife Speciality Hospital,
wherein she took treatment as inpatient from 17.07.2022 to 18.07.2022, medical certificate marked as Ex.P.18, medical bills amounting to Rs.26,38,712/- marked as SCCH 5 Ex.P.23, advance receipts marked as Ex.P.24 and medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.25.
On perusal of the said medical bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for the treatment of the deceased is considered.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for the said medical bills.
The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No.
Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 22,30,200-00 2. Loss of filial consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.1 and 2)
3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 5.
Medical Expenses 26,38,712-00 Total 49,38,912-00 33.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.49,38,912/-
with SCCH 5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
34.
In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Honda Activa brKA-52-Q-8726 has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 vide policy bearing No.v9926349 which is valid from 18.03.2022 to 17.03.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.06.2022, hence as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
So that, respondent No.2/insurer of the Honda Activa is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.49,38,912/- (Rupees Forty Nine Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand Nine Hundred Twelve Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.
The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
